html:
SMTO-SKL-0104 — Your Microsoft account hasn't allowed this kind of access yet

GUID: 6f6cf3b8-df6c-5d7b-ae65-e19b71682e92
Slug: microsoft365-scope-missing
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • When you connected this Microsoft account, you didn't allow the access this action needs, such as sending mail or changing files. SMTO didn't try the action.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to reconnect the same Microsoft 365 account and add the missing access shown in this error. Reconnecting with more access keeps the permissions you already gave.
  2. Open the sign-in link, sign in with the same account, and read the permission list before approving it. Microsoft shows exactly what SMTO will be allowed to do.
  3. After it connects, ask the Agent to do your request again. With the new access in place, it's safe to try the request again.

What success looks like

  • The browser page says your account is connected and the Agent completes your request.

If it still fails

  • If Microsoft says an administrator must approve, ask your Microsoft administrator. Otherwise select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • require_features found that the selected Microsoft 365 account's granted delegated scopes do not cover the operation's required features; the error lists missing_features and required_scopes.

What this means

  • Required operation features map to delegated scopes absent from the account's granted scope set. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Required operation features map to delegated scopes absent from the account's granted scope set.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect missing_features and the exact delegated scopes they require.

How to fix it

  • Call microsoft365.connect with the same auth_app_ref and account_key, adding the reported missing_features. Review the required_scopes before consent; tenant policy may require administrator consent for some delegated scopes (for example Sites.Read.All).
  • Reconnect the same account_key with microsoft365.connect and the reported missing_features. Review the exact delegated scopes before consent.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The same account deliberately grants the necessary feature through supported consent.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
